title: Xception: Deep Learning with Depthwise Separable Convolutions

numbers.sentence: FastEval14k is a dataset of 14,000 images with dense annotations from about 6,000 classes (36.5 labels per image on average).
Learning rate decay: decay of rate 0.94 every 2 epochs
Learning rate decay: decay of rate 0.9 every 3,000,000 samples
Dropout: For the ImageNet experiments, both models include a dropout layer of rate 0.5 before the logistic regression layer.
On JFT, Xception shows a 4.3% relative improvement on the FastEval14k MAP@100 metric.
Both architectures have approximately the same size (within 3.5%), and Xception is marginally slower.
Learning rate decay: decay of rate 0.94 every 2 epochs
The ImageNet experiments took approximately 3 days each, while the JFT experiments took over one month each.

assumptions.sentence: We believe this may be due to the fact that Inception V3 was developed with a focus on ImageNet and may thus be by design over-fit to this specific task.

assumptions.sentence: It is likely that a search for better hyperparameters for Xception on ImageNet (in particular optimization parameters and regularization parameters) would yield significant additional improvement.

assumptions.sentence: We expect that engineering optimizations at the level of the depthwise convolution operations can make Xception faster than Inception V3 in the near future.
assumptions.anchorText: We expect that engineering optimizations at the level of the depthwise convolution operations can make Xception faster than Inception V3 in the near future.

assumptions.sentence: We expect depthwise separable convolutions to become a cornerstone of convolutional neural network architecture design in the future, since they offer similar properties as Inception modules, yet are as easy to use as regular convolution layers.
